claim: Distinct gp120s stabilize different CCR5 conformations.

claim: GPCRs constitute one of the primary drug target classes.

claim: GPCRs exist in different subpopulations at the cell surface due to arrangements of receptor loops and transmembrane domains.

claim: The degree of receptor oligomerization contributes to the stability of CCR5 molecules at the cell surface.
source: These data suggested that the degree of receptor oligomerization contributed to the stability of CCR5 molecules at the cell surface, as previously proposed (Calebiro et al., 2012).

claim: PTX treatment did not alter the proportion of the eGFP-CCR5-L196K restricted tracklets pool.

evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Most of eGFP-CCR5-L196K are not precoupled to the Gi protein at the basal state.

evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the PTX experiments with L196K.

claim: There could be a link between dimerization and Gi coupling at basal state.

evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: eGFP-CCR5-L196K was only slightly immobilized after 10 min of PSC-RANTES treatment.
source: Contrary to eGFP-CCR5-WT massive immobilization and clustering upon PSC-RANTES treatment (Figure 3A–B), eGFP-CCR5-L196K was only slightly immobilized after 10 min of treatment (Figure 5E–F)
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: Large immobile spots were not detected for eGFP-CCR5-L196K after PSC-RANTES treatment.
source: while large immobile spots were not detected (Video 7).
evidence: This is an observation stated in the results and shown in a video.

claim: CCR5 immobilization and clustering after stimulation depend on CCR5 dimerization.
source: This result indicated that CCR5 immobilization and clustering after stimulation depend on CCR5 dimerization.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the L196K experiments.

claim: The proportion of recruited βarr2-GFP at the plasma membrane was similar for CCR5-WT and CCR5-L196K.
source: The proportion of recruited βarr2-GFP at the plasma membrane was similar for CCR5-WT and CCR5-L196K (Figure 6B), suggesting that βarr2 recruitment is independent of the oligomeric status of the receptor.

claim: βarr2 recruitment is independent of the oligomeric status of the receptor.
source: The proportion of recruited βarr2-GFP at the plasma membrane was similar for CCR5-WT and CCR5-L196K (Figure 6B), suggesting that βarr2 recruitment is independent of the oligomeric status of the receptor.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the βarr2 recruitment experiments.

claim: A slight decrease in the number of βarr2-GFP spots that colocalize with fluorescent receptor spots was observed in CCR5-L196K expressing cells compared to CCR5-WT expressing cells.

claim: The lack of immobilization and clustering of activated CCR5-L196K is not due to a default of βarr2 recruitment.

evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the βarr2 recruitment experiments.

claim: CCR5 dimerization impacts its internalization process.
source: A saturating concentration of PSC-RANTES decreased cell surface expression of both receptors, but not in the same proportion (Figure 6C), suggesting that CCR5 dimerization impacted its internalization process.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Dimerization regulates activated receptor mobility and internalization.
source: These results supported that dimerization regulated activated receptor mobility and internalization.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the internalization experiments.

claim: While dimerization is a pre-requisite to the immobilization of the receptor, it is not essential for receptor internalization.
source: Note that, while dimerization is a pre-requisite to the immobilization of the receptor, it was not essential for receptor internalization.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the comparison of immobilization and internalization data.

claim: Receptor massive immobilization is not an absolute requirement for receptor internalization.
source: This suggests that receptor massive immobilization is not an absolute requirement for receptor internalization.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the L196K internalization data.

claim: Twenty min of gp120 exposure slightly modulated the mobility of eGFP-CCR5-WT, although this trend was not statistically significant.
source: Twenty min of gp120 exposure slightly modulated the mobility of eGFP-CCR5-WT (and FLAG-ST-CCR5-WT), although this trend was not statistically significant (Figure 7A and C) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 7.

claim: HIV-1 gp120s immobilized eGFP-CCR5-L196K, with gp #34 having the highest effect.

evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: gp120s stabilize CCR5 conformations that are different from those stabilized by chemokines.
source: This suggested (i) that gp120s stabilized CCR5 conformations, which were different from those stabilized by chemokines
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the differential effects of gp120s vs chemokines.

claim: Different envelopes stabilize differently CCR5 conformations.
source: and (ii) that different envelopes also stabilized differently CCR5 conformations, in accordance with our previous result (Colin et al., 2013; Colin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Quantitative analysis of the motion of CCR5 particles revealed two classes of receptor trajectories in the basal state: Brownian and restricted.
source: Quantitative analysis of the motion of CCR5 particles and their composition within the fluorescent spots present at the cell membrane of HEK 293 cells revealed in the basal state (i) two classes of receptor trajectories, Brownian and restricted (Figure 2)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and refers to data in Figure 2.

claim: CCR5 exists in different oligomeric states with low (50%), medium (40%), and high fluorescence intensity (10%).
source: and (ii) different oligomeric states (Figure 5) with low (50 %), medium (40 %), and high fluorescence intensity (10 %).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and refers to data in Figure 5.

claim: The change in mobility between periods of confinement separated by free diffusion could be attributed to the molecular organization of the receptor oscillating between different oligomeric forms at the cell surface.
source: The change in mobility between periods of confinement separated by free diffusion could be attributed to the molecular organization of the receptor oscillating between different oligomeric forms at the cell surface (monomers, dimers, oligomers), as proposed for CCR5 (Jin et al., 2018) or other receptors (Möller et al., 2020; Kasai et al., 2018; Martínez-Muñoz et al., 2018; Tabor et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Change in CCR5 mobility could be linked to a transient association of the receptor with the cytoskeleton.
source: Change in mobility could also be linked to a transient association of the receptor with the cytoskeleton regardless of its oligomeric status (Calebiro and Koszegi, 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a possible explanation and supported by a citation.

claim: Change in CCR5 mobility could be linked to transient coupling to G proteins.
source: and/or to transient coupling to G proteins, leading to a transient immobility of the receptor in the basal state.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a possible explanation.

claim: An active receptor-G protein complex is formed in a confined region of the plasma membrane at the basal state and lasts around 1 s.
source: These data are consistent with dual-color TIRF-M analysis of adrenergic receptor and G protein, showing that an active receptor-G protein complex is formed in a confined region of the plasma membrane at the basal state and lasts around 1 s (Sungkaworn et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Dynamics of distinct GPCRs can be differently impacted by coupling to G proteins.
source: However, they contrast with a study on mGluR3 showing higher mobility of the receptor when complexed with G protein (Yanagawa et al., 2018). This suggested that dynamics of distinct GPCRs can be differently impacted by coupling to G proteins.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion based on comparison with other studies.

claim: CCR5 is not precoupled to β-arrestins in its basal state.
source: Regarding β-arrestin association, we showed using siRNA that CCR5 was not precoupled to β-arrestins in its basal state (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and refers to data in Figure 4C.

claim: CCR5 conformations that bind to G proteins are not recognized by β-arrestins.
source: This result suggests that CCR5 conformations, which bind to G proteins are not recognized by β-arrestins.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion based on the siRNA experiments.

claim: The conformations of receptors interacting with G proteins and β-arrestins are different.
source: This is consistent with the idea that the conformations of receptors interacting with G proteins and β-arrestins are different (Lagane et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Characterizing ligands by their impact on receptor motion opens a new way to classify biased ligands.
source: Therefore, characterizing ligands by their impact on receptor motion opens a new way to classify biased ligands.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the differential effects of ligands.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of the CD4-gp120-CCR5 complex shows that CCR5 adopts inactive conformation.
source: This feature contrasts with the cryo-EM structure of the CD4-gp120-CCR5 complex, showing that CCR5 adopts inactive confomation (Shaik et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: gp120 binding reorients characteristic microswitches involved in GPCR activation.
source: However, it is in line with gp120s-induced CCR5 signaling (Brelot and Chakrabarti, 2018; Flanagan, 2014) and with recent MD simulations showing that gp120 binding reorients characteric microswitches involved in GPCR activation (Jacquemard et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Receptor dimerization may regulate precoupling of CCR5 to Gi proteins.
source: Our results suggest that receptor dimerization may regulate precoupling of CCR5 to Gi proteins.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion based on the L196K and PTX experiments.

claim: Most eGFP-CCR5-L196K receptors that reside preferentially as monomers are not coupled to Gi proteins in the basal state.
source: This suggests that most eGFP-CCR5-L196K receptors that reside preferentially as monomers are not coupled to Gi proteins in the basal state, in agreement with previous conclusion on CXCR4 (Möller et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Dimerization is a pre-requisite to receptor immobilization and clustering upon activation by chemokine agonists.
source: Our analysis suggests that dimerization is a pre-requisite to receptor immobilization and clustering upon activation by chemokine agonists.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion based on the L196K experiments.

claim: Receptor immobility and clustering are independent of Gi protein coupling.
source: This result is not due to impaired binding of the chemokine, because we controlled that PSC-RANTES induced efficient ERK1/2 activation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and endocytosis of the mutant receptor (Figure 6C). Receptor immobility and clustering were independent of Gi protein coupling, as exemplified by unaffected CCR5 mobility after 10 min of agonist stimulation in PTX pre-treated cells (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and refers to data in Figures 4B, 5, and 6C.

claim: Receptor immobility and clustering are most likely related to uncoupled and desensitized form of CCR5 that accumulate in CCS (clathrin-coated structures).
source: but most likely related to uncoupled and desensitized form of CCR5 that accumulate in CCS (clathrin-coated structures), as proposed (Grove et al., 2014; Yanagawa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation and supported by citations.

claim: β-arrestins recruitment depends on the efficiency of ligand to trigger CCR5 internalization.
source: This hypothesis was strengthened with the essential role of β-arrestins in activated receptor immobility and clustering (Figure 4D; Markova et al., 2021) and with studies showing that β-arrestins recruitment depends on the efficiency of ligand to trigger CCR5 internalization (Jin et al., 2018; Tarancón Díez et al., 2014; Truan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Activated receptor clustering may correspond to an accumulation of receptor in early endosome for a second phase of activation.

evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation and supported by a citation.

evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Receptor oligomerization might be an essential requirement for β-arrestins to trigger receptor clustering and immobilization.
source: We propose a model in which receptor oligomerization might be an essential requirement for β-arrestins to trigger receptor clustering and immobilization.
evidence: This is a model proposed in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: A concerted self-association of arrestins may favor receptor clustering and immobilization.
source: A concerted self-association of arrestins may favor this process (Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation and supported by a citation.

claim: PSC-RANTES induces strong β-arrestins clustering.
source: Indeed, PSC-RANTES induces strong β-arrestins clustering (Tarancón Díez et al., 2014; Truan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

source: We speculate that the co-clustering of β−arrestins with receptors may serve as a platform helping to concentrate cargo for optimal and productive internalization.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation.

claim: GPCR monomers can be active enough on their own to be functional.

evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the overall findings.
